title: Rigveda 1.14: To all the gods
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.14: To all the gods: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.14 is a hymn of 12 verses addressed to all the gods. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 7v-8r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.14.1-2 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 1, varga 26); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 7v
translation.original_text:
1aibhi̍r agne̱ duvo̱ giro̱ viśve̍bhi̱ḥ soma̍pītaye | de̱vebhi̍r yāhi̱ yakṣi̍ ca ||
2ā tvā̱ kaṇvā̍ ahūṣata gṛ̱ṇanti̍ vipra te̱ dhiya̍ḥ | de̱vebhi̍r agna̱ ā ga̍hi ||
translation.text:
1To drink the Soma, Agni, come, to our service and our songs. With all these Gods; and worship them.
2The Kaṇvas have invoked thee; they, O Singer, sing thee songs of praise Agni, come hither with the Gods;
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 7v (OPenn image 9, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.13.4 ‹devān iḷitaḥ ā vaha›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 8r, begins in RV 1.14.3 ‹-mitrā agnim pūṣaṇam bhagam›. Verses 1.14.1-2 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 1.14.3-12 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 1, varga 26); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 8r
translation.original_text:
3i̱ndra̱vā̱yū bṛha̱spati̍m mi̱trāgnim pū̱ṣaṇa̱m bhaga̍m | ā̱di̱tyān māru̍taṁ ga̱ṇam ||
4pra vo̍ bhriyanta̱ inda̍vo matsa̱rā mā̍dayi̱ṣṇava̍ḥ | dra̱psā madhva̍ś camū̱ṣada̍ḥ ||
5īḻa̍te̱ tvām a̍va̱syava̱ḥ kaṇvā̍so vṛ̱ktaba̍rhiṣaḥ | ha̱viṣma̍nto ara̱ṁkṛta̍ḥ ||
6ghṛ̱tapṛ̍ṣṭhā mano̱yujo̱ ye tvā̱ vaha̍nti̱ vahna̍yaḥ | ā de̱vān soma̍pītaye ||
7tān yaja̍trām̐ ṛtā̱vṛdho 'gne̱ patnī̍vatas kṛdhi | madhva̍ḥ sujihva pāyaya ||
8ye yaja̍trā̱ ya īḍyā̱s te te̍ pibantu ji̱hvayā̍ | madho̍r agne̱ vaṣa̍ṭkṛti ||
9ākī̱ṁ sūrya̍sya roca̱nād viśvā̍n de̱vām̐ u̍ṣa̱rbudha̍ḥ | vipro̱ hote̱ha va̍kṣati ||
10viśve̍bhiḥ so̱myam madhv agna̱ indre̍ṇa vā̱yunā̍ | pibā̍ mi̱trasya̱ dhāma̍bhiḥ ||
11tvaṁ hotā̱ manu̍rhi̱to 'gne̍ ya̱jñeṣu̍ sīdasi | semaṁ no̍ adhva̱raṁ ya̍ja ||
12yu̱kṣvā hy aru̍ṣī̱ rathe̍ ha̱rito̍ deva ro̱hita̍ḥ | tābhi̍r de̱vām̐ i̱hā va̍ha ||
translation.text:
3Indra, Vâyu, Br̥ihaspati, Mitra, Agni, Pûshan, Bhaga, Âdityas, and the Marut host.
4For you these juices are poured forth that gladden and exhilarate, The meath-drops resting in the cup.
5The sons of Kaṇva fain for help adore thee, having strewn the grass, With offerings and all things prepared.
6Let the swift steeds who carry thee, thought-yoked and dropping holy oil, Bring the Gods to the Soma draught.
7Adored, the strengtheners of Law, unite them, Agni, with their Dames: Make them drink meath, O bright of tongue.
8Let them, O Agni, who deserve worship and praise drink with thy tongue The meath in solemn sacrifice.
9Away, from the Sun's realm of light, the wise invoking Priest shall bring All Gods awaking with the dawn.
10With all the Gods, with Indra, with Vâyu, and Mitra's splendours, drink, Agni, the pleasant Soma juice.
11Ordained by Manu as our Priest, thou sittest, Agni, at each rite: Hallow thou this our sacrifice.
12Harness the Red Mares to thy car, the Bays, O God, the flaming ones: With those bring hitherward the Gods.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 8r (OPenn image 9, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.14.3 ‹-mitrā agnim pūṣaṇam bhagam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 8v, begins in RV 1.15.2 ‹ṛtunā potrāt yajñam pūnītana›. Verses 1.14.3-12 end on this page; 1.14.3 begins on fol. 7v.
